evidence.quote: allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict

criteria.reasoning: Primary mission and need well described with refs. Single-sat rationale given. Operator vs customers not distinguished; operated from Australia facilities vague. Missing clear operator/customer identification.

evidence.quote: launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 87.7924°

criteria.reasoning: All sub-sections covered with STK screenshots and access table. Multiple technical errors: inclination 87.79 not SSO, sma 7171km wrong, Kourou latitude 45.05N, contact duration misread, RAAN logic flawed. No STK files evidenced.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.

criteria.reasoning: Summarises launch, orbit, ground station and benefit. Largely restates design with caveat on Vega E. Lacks detailed evidence-based conclusions or quantified performance.
Clear headings, exec summary, readable writing. Figures have minimal captions, inconsistent numbering. References use bare URLs and include Wikipedia which brief forbids. Formatting inconsistent.

technical_issues.issue: SSO inclination at 600km quoted as 87.79 deg; correct ~97.8 deg as per own plot. 87.79 deg is prograde and not sun-synchronous.
Kourou latitude quoted as 45.05 deg N; actual ~5.2 deg N. Invalidates two-windows-per-day argument detail.
Mean access 580.786s (~9.7 min) described as almost twenty minutes; misinterpretation by factor 2.
RAAN 27.33 deg claimed to indicate launch facility location; RAAN does not equal launch longitude and explanation of J2 precession incomplete.

overall: Single-sat reef monitor concept well motivated. Design covers all segments with STK evidence but contains significant orbital-mechanics numerical errors and weak referencing.
